items.title: BREAKING: Nvidia Leads 50 Companies Against White House's AI Model Crackdown
items.summary:
Two days after the White House accused a Chinese lab of stealing from Anthropic's Fable model, Nvidia led a coalition, initially 25 companies and expanded to 50 within days, arguing the opposite: that the technique behind the accusation is standard practice, not theft. Signatories include Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, Hugging Face, Andreessen Horowitz, and the Linux Foundation, later joined by Google, OpenAI, and AMD. Notably absent: Anthropic and Amazon.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down Jensen Huang's open letter defending distillation as a "widely used technique for model improvement," why the letter never names China, Moonshot, or DeepSeek even once, and why Nvidia's position isn't purely philosophical, since more open models mean more GPU demand either way.

The group blames the breach on a single weak password, and the download link was reportedly still active when researchers checked.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down why Bank of Baroda, the RBI, and CERT-In have stayed largely silent, how this lands the same week as a separate accounting charge hitting the bank's stock, and what it means when a breach at this scale touches over 180 million customers, whether or not it's ever independently confirmed.

Note: These are unverified allegations from the hacking group; none of the claims has been independently confirmed by Bank of Baroda, the RBI, or CERT-In as of publishing.

items.title: TRAP: India Is Training the Robots That Could Replace Its Workers | Point Break
items.summary:
Physical AI is creating a new global demand for human movement, judgement and skill. India has the scale and diversity to supply that training data, but the value, ownership and protection of the workers creating it remain unresolved. 

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Mythily Ramesh - Co-Founder & MD at Next Wealth, Manish Agarwal - Co-Founder of Humyn Labs and Saravanan Balasundaram Founder & CEO of Han Digital Solutions, to break down why robots need real-world multisensory human data, how Indian workers are training physical AI systems, why India could become a global AI factory, and whether the country is repeating the outsourcing pattern of call centres and data annotation. The conversation examines robotic training across farms, factories, warehouses, and homes; the role of behavioural intelligence; the growth of machine learning operations; the potential expansion of India’s physical AI workforce from 2.5 lakh to 10 lakh by 2032; and the rise of teleoperation as a new opportunity for skilled Indian workers. It also explores the Amazon Go human-in-the-loop debate, worker consent and disclosure, privacy, data ownership, physical intelligence as a new asset class, and whether India can build its own intelligence layer instead of remaining a low-cost service provider for foreign AI companies.
